cards.title: Avoid branded product-page imagery when dropshipping unbranded items
cards.claim: When using a dropshipping supplier’s product, displaying branding on the product page can create a mismatch between what customers see and receive.
cards.action: Use the dropshipping supplier’s images for product pages; keep the brand work visible on the website rather than on product pages until the branded product is available.
applies_when: You are dropshipping because you cannot yet fund inventory, branding, and packaging.
The supplied product will not carry your branding.
do_not_use_when: The received product and packaging match the branding shown on the product page.
unknowns: No customer-impact or conversion result is provided.
The passage does not specify which website areas should show the branding.
evidence_quotes: "then go and drop ship it and use this supplier, your drop shipping suppliers images to create all of the images for your brand."

"But still, the branding that you've done, um, that should be very visible on the website, not on the product pages, cuz then there'll be a mismatch between the product that they receive versus the one that they see."

cards.title: Stage sourcing from dropshipping to private labeling
cards.claim: The described sourcing report recommends beginning with dropshipping, moving to Zenrop or Spocket after initial orders for faster delivery, and moving to private labeling after more sales.
cards.action: Start with dropshipping; after getting some orders, consider Zenrop or Spocket for faster delivery; after more sales, move into private labeling.
applies_when: You are following the sourcing report’s recommendation for the featured product.
You need to start before funding inventory and private-label packaging.
do_not_use_when: A supplier, product category, compliance requirement, or economics calls for a different sourcing approach.
unknowns: The order and sales thresholds are not specified.

cards.title: Decide whether the page is transactional before mirroring it
cards.claim: The page-mirroring workflow distinguishes pages where people buy from pages with other functions, because buying pages need checkout-related elements.
cards.action: Choose whether people buy on the page before mirroring it; include checkout-related elements when people buy on that page.

unknowns: The passage does not define which checkout elements are included.
